nota: 'Systemic envenoming occurred in 835 patients (54%; median, 87 patients per year; IQR, 62–102 per year'. A média e a mediana ficam abaixo de 100, mas o quartil de cima é 102: em parte dos anos passou de 100. A voz diz 'fewer than a hundred bites a year': é verdade na média, não em todo ano. A tela pode levar 'ON AVERAGE' (o redator decide). F131/F133: 'Snake envenoming is infrequent in Australia, and much less common than previous annual estimates suggested'.

texto_aprovado: You might be thinking: that's the antivenom. Partly. The answer starts before any hospital, though. In Australia, a snake actually putting venom into a person is rare to begin with. That same national study found fewer than a hundred bites a year that injected venom, far fewer than earlier estimates had suggested.
